findings_from_the_oracle: The oracle went red on ITSELF twice before it went red on the world, and both are recorded in its header rather than quietly fixed: (a) I1 charged 27 violations on `kill_some > rest > kill_some` because the payment key was the body-life and not the body-life PER REST EPOCH -- RI-PRG06 s4's respawn row says a rest makes the same body payable again; (b) I3 charged 45 violations on `kill_some > release > materialise` because the oracle drove bare harness verbs instead of PopulationSystem's own release/_materialise, i.e. it was auditing a route the world does not have.

AFTER those two corrections, 460 of 463 routes clean and 17 I3 violations on 2 distinct routes NOBODY HAS EVER DRIVEN: `kill_some > release > materialise > materialise > materialise` and `save_load > kill_all > materialise > release > materialise`. Both materialise a post that is already standing.

ROOT: Engine.spawnEncounter() IS NOT ATOMIC. It spawns members in order and Engine.spawn() THROWS on a duplicate eid, so a post whose survivor is still standing spawns every member before it -- alive, full HP, including the ones the player killed -- and then throws. _materialise's catch marks the post CLEARED and returns, leaving those bodies in the world and in nothing's index. Untracked, live, free.

Not reachable by a player today: step (4) guarantees DORMANT before calling _materialise. But that guarantee lives in the CALLER, which is the exact shape of defect this whole round is about, so _materialise is now idempotent -- a post whose bodies are already in the world is not materialised. This is what 'make the fourth instance impossible rather than absent' bought.
